Section 1: Company Overview & Audited Financial Baseline

The Core Business Machine, Moat & Unit Economics

Primary Economic Moat Rating: Narrow Moat (Nationwide 1,600+ Warehouse Fulfillment Scale & B2B Procurement Leverage).

JD.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: JD) operates as China’s largest direct retailer and supply chain infrastructure titan (converted at an exchange rate of RMB 7.00 / $1.00 USD; 1 ADS = 2 Class A Ordinary Shares). Unlike asset-light marketplace aggregators that rely on third-party merchant fulfillment, JD’s foundational business architecture was engineered on a direct, first-party (1P) procurement and nationwide self-operated logistics backbone. The company purchases inventory at scale directly from brand manufacturers, manages end-to-end warehousing, and executes last-mile delivery through its captive logistics network (JD Logistics). Over two decades, this capital-intensive strategy has established a nearly insurmountable competitive barrier across mainland China.

Following H1 2026 share repurchases, JD's capital structure is synchronized at 1,340.0M diluted US-listed ADSs outstanding (equivalent to 2,680.0M Class A/B Ordinary Shares). This reduction in capital count enhances per-share fundamental density across all cash flow and valuation metrics.

JD operates within the classic Efficient Scale and Cost Advantage moat archetypes. By operating over 1,600 self-managed warehouses spanning more than 32 million square meters of aggregate floor area, JD has created a fulfillment tollbridge that cannot be replicated without tens of billions of dollars in sunk capital and decades of land-use approvals. This scale generates extreme purchasing leverage over suppliers, enabling JD to secure the lowest procurement costs in consumer electronics, home appliances, and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). The resulting unit cost per parcel delivered is among the lowest in the industry, creating a virtuous flywheel: lower delivery costs lead to lower retail prices, driving higher order volume, which amortizes fixed warehouse infrastructure across greater volume.

Monetization Mechanics & Revenue Engines:

  • JD Retail (1P Direct Sales & 3P Platform): Generates revenue through direct merchandise markup on electronics, home appliances, and general merchandise (1P), as well as take-rate commissions, platform transaction fees, and high-margin digital advertising from third-party (3P) merchants operating on the JD marketplace.
  • JD Logistics (JDL): Monetizes internal fulfillment scale by offering end-to-end supply chain solutions, express delivery, freight transportation, and cold-chain logistics to external enterprise clients, converting a cost center into a stand-alone profit center.
  • New Businesses & JD Health: Encompasses retail pharmacies, telemedicine consultations, wholesale healthcare distribution, international cross-border e-commerce (Ochama), and local on-demand retail/food delivery initiatives.

Buffett & Munger Pricing Power & Inflation Resistance Audit

Pricing Power Classification: Constrained Pricing Power / Cost Advantage Pass-Through. Under Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger’s underwriting lens, JD does not possess "Absolute Pricing Power" (the ability to raise end-consumer retail prices arbitrarily without suffering volume destruction). In standard consumer retail, JD is subject to intense e-commerce price competition. However, JD possesses an exceptional form of B2B Procurement Pricing Power and Fulfillment Cost Advantage: because JD is often the single largest distribution channel for major global and domestic consumer electronics brands, it dictates payment terms, volume rebates, and wholesale purchasing discounts.

The 'Prayer Session' Test: In consumer-facing 1P retail, JD cannot unilaterally hike retail prices above competitors like Alibaba or Pinduoduo without facing immediate basket abandonment. Rather than pricing above the market, JD competes on speed, authenticity, and customer experience. When input costs rise, JD passes cost increases upstream to manufacturers through wholesale contract negotiations and downstream via dynamic retail repricing, preventing gross margin degradation.

Customer Share of Wallet & Value Surplus: JD represents a high share of wallet for high-ticket household purchases (laptops, smartphones, refrigerators, HVAC systems). The consumer value surplus stems from guaranteed authentic merchandise (zero tolerance for counterfeits) and reliable same-day / next-day delivery ("211 Program"), which creates high customer loyalty among China's middle-to-upper-tier urban demographics.

3-Year Audited Gross Margin Resilience: Despite deflationary headwinds and fierce e-commerce price matching, JD expanded its gross profit margin consistently across the last three fiscal years, demonstrating structural operating discipline and supply chain efficiencies.

Inflation Capital Intensity: As noted in Buffett’s 1981 shareholder letter, an inflation-resistant enterprise must expand earnings without requiring massive incremental capital expenditures. JD has largely passed its peak warehouse footprint buildout cycle. Incremental revenue from high-margin 3P marketplace take-rates and advertising drops directly to operating cash flow without necessitating proportional warehouse square footage expansion.

4-Quarter Operating Reality & Management Call Commentary

A synthesis of statutory filings and earnings calls across the trailing four quarters (Q3 2025 through Q2 2026) reveals steady operational execution amidst a bifurcated macroeconomic landscape and notable product category shifts:

  • Q3 2025: Net revenue reached $42.73B (RMB 299.1B), up 14.9% YoY. JD Retail operating margin expanded to 5.9% (vs. 5.2% in Q3 2024). Annual active customer accounts crossed 700 million. Management highlighted strong user engagement and sequential reduction in New Business operating losses.
  • Q4 2025: Net revenue reached $50.33B (RMB 352.3B), up 1.5% YoY against a strong prior-year baseline. General merchandise sales grew 12.1% YoY, offsetting short-term consumer electronics softness. Management completed $3.0B in share repurchases in FY 2025 (retiring 6.3% of shares) and declared a $1.2B annual cash dividend.
  • Q1 2026: Net revenue rose to $43.01B (RMB 301.1B), driven by accelerated 3P merchant ecosystem expansion and JD Logistics efficiency gains. JD Retail operating income expanded as high-margin advertising grew double digits. Local on-demand delivery services were integrated directly into JD Logistics to serve 3P platform merchants.
  • Q2 2026 Category Mix & Operating Realities: Net revenue was $49.49B (RMB 346.4B), down 2.9% YoY due to post-subsidy durables normalization following peak government trade-in incentives in Q2 2025. Crucially, category mix dynamics bifurcated: 1P Electronics and Home Appliances contracted by -11.8% YoY as high-ticket discretionary purchases normalized, while General Merchandise and FMCG expanded by a compensating +5.6% YoY, demonstrating non-discretionary basket resilience. Concurrently, New Businesses incurred a heavy operating drag with a quarterly operating loss of RMB 9.9B ($1.41B), driven by front-loaded capital expenditures in European retail fulfillment (Ochama) and local food delivery infrastructure expansion. Despite this drag, consolidated trailing twelve-month Free Cash Flow reached $7.30B, and management executed $1.0B in share repurchases during H1 2026, reducing the diluted share count to 1,340M ADSs.

Useful Lives & Maintenance CapEx Disclosures: As disclosed in Note 1 of Form 20-F, JD depreciates electronic servers and software over 3 to 5 years, logistics equipment and vehicles over 5 to 10 years, and warehouse structures over 20 to 40 years. Total capital expenditures across LTM Q2 2026 were $2,566M (RMB 17.96B), which includes heavy growth CapEx for development properties ($1,160M) and logistics hub expansions. Discretionary growth spending is segregated from steady-state Maintenance CapEx, which is calibrated at $1,050M (~35% of total D&A) to sustain existing warehouse equipment and IT infrastructure.

Foreign Private Issuer (FPI), VIE Architecture & Upstream Cash Repatriation

JD.com, Inc. is an exempted holding company incorporated in the Cayman Islands. Due to Chinese legal restrictions on foreign ownership in value-added telecommunications services and retail pharmacy licenses, domestic operating assets are partially held via Variable Interest Entities (VIEs), including Beijing Jingdong 360 Degree E-Commerce Co., Ltd.. The overwhelming majority of operating cash flows and hard logistics real estate are directly owned through wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOEs) rather than contractual VIEs.

Upstream Cash Remittance Mechanics: Cash generated by operating subsidiaries is remitted to the offshore Cayman holding company via intercompany consulting services, software licensing fees, and formal board-declared dividends. Under PRC tax law, enterprise dividend distributions to offshore parent companies are subject to a 10% withholding tax (reduced to 5% under the Hong Kong-Mainland double-tax treaty). As proven by the $3.0B share repurchase execution in FY 2025 and $1.0B in H1 2026, JD possesses uninhibited operational ability to upstream billions of dollars in RMB, convert funds into USD/HKD via SAFE-compliant channels, and retire US-listed ADSs.

Historical Corporate Trauma & Structural Remediation

JD's equity has historically suffered severe drawdowns (>60% from peak levels) driven by three structural traumas:

  1. Aggressive Pricing Wars & Subsidy Drag (2022–2024): Rapid consumer migration toward deep-discount platforms pressured top-line growth, prompting JD to launch a RMB 10B subsidy campaign. Structural Fix: JD reoriented capital allocation toward ROI-driven retail efficiency, opened its logistics infrastructure to 3P merchants to expand product selection across lower price tiers, and curtailed loss-making community group-buying (Jingxi) ventures, stabilizing consolidated retail operating margins at 4.6%–5.0%.
  2. Founder Governance & Key-Person Concentration (2018–2022): Heightened headline risk surrounding founder voting control created governance discounts. Structural Fix: Institutionalized professional management was established under CEO Sandy Xu and CFO Ian Su Shan. Independent board oversight was expanded, strategic decision-making was decentralized across business units, and transparent annual capital return programs were codified.
  3. New Businesses Capital Losses & Overseas Drag (2025–2026): Uncontrolled capital allocation to international cross-border logistics and quick-commerce food delivery caused severe quarterly margin dilution (RMB 9.9B loss in Q2 2026). Structural Fix: Management implemented disciplined investment caps, anchoring New Businesses operating loss containment targets below RMB 7.5B per quarter, while automating merchant operations via AI tools (JoyInsight, JD Streamer) across 40,000+ sellers to drive core retail margin expansion.

Section 2: The Three Forward-Looking Operating Stories

Based on JD.com's core retail premise, reported operational metrics, financial filings, and recent earnings trajectories, here are three distinct, probable fundamental operating paths covering 90%–95% of realistic corporate outcomes over the next 3–5 years, fully benchmarked against a baseline Starting Owner Earnings (\(OE_0\)) of $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS on 1,340M diluted ADSs) and Net Surplus Cash of $22,534M ($16.82 per ADS):

📖 Story 1: Mature Supply Chain Compounding & 3P Monetization (Base Case)

In this baseline operating trajectory, JD leverages its entrenched national logistics infrastructure to compound earnings at a steady GDP-plus pace while pivoting incremental Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) toward its high-margin third-party (3P) marketplace. Following the expiration of government trade-in subsidies—which drove a -11.8% YoY contraction in 1P Electronics and Appliances in Q2 2026—durables demand normalizes into low single-digit volume growth. This temporary 1P headwind is fully compensated by persistent +5.6% YoY expansion in General Merchandise, FMCG, and supermarket categories, reflecting structural shopping frequency gains.

Crucially, 3P marketplace monetization accelerates through the deployment of merchant AI productivity tools (JoyInsight for automated ad bidding and inventory prediction, and JD Streamer for autonomous live-streaming avatars) across 40,000+ active sellers. These AI tools increase merchant ROI and ad velocity, driving 3P marketplace take-rates higher. Concurrently, management exercises strict capital discipline over New Businesses: the recent operational drag (which reached an RMB 9.9B loss in Q2 2026 due to overseas logistics expansion and local food delivery trials) is reined in, establishing a firm loss ceiling below RMB 7.5B per quarter before trending downward toward RMB 2.5B–3.0B annually by Year 5.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Annual active customer accounts expand modestly from 700 million to 760 million (1.6% CAGR), with annual spend per active customer climbing to $295 USD. The 3P marketplace ad revenue and commission share expands from 7.3% ($14.7B) to 9.5% ($21.5B) of consolidated revenue. Net revenue grows at a 3.8% organic CAGR, rising from $187.6B LTM to $226.0B USD by Year 5.

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Gross profit margin expands from 16.59% to 17.60% by Year 5, driven by high-margin 3P ad streams and AI-driven warehouse automation. Consolidated GAAP operating margin expands to 3.20% ($7.23B). CapEx efficiency remains high: Maintenance CapEx is capped at $1,150M USD (~35% of total D&A), and Stock-Based Compensation is stabilized at $700M USD. With a negative Cash Conversion Cycle (-16 to -18 days) preserving float, Core Operating Owner Earnings compound from $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS on 1,340M ADSs) to $6,150M USD ($4.59 per ADS before buyback retirements; ~$5.35 per ADS assuming continued $2B annual share repurchases). Net Surplus Cash ($22,534M / $16.82 per ADS) provides an unencumbered liquidity anchor.

Key Milestones to Watch: 3P ad revenue sustained at >10% YoY growth; adoption of JoyInsight and JD Streamer surpassing 60,000 merchants; New Businesses quarterly operating loss kept strictly below RMB 7.5B; net share count declining 3%–4% annually below the 1,340M ADS baseline.

📖 Story 2: Platform Monetization Flywheel & Automated Logistics Leverage (Bull Case)

In this upside operational trajectory, JD executes a high-margin platform transformation. Post-subsidy durables demand rebounds into a premium upgrade cycle, while General Merchandise accelerates beyond +8.0% YoY. The core catalyst is the viral adoption of merchant AI productivity suites (JoyInsight and JD Streamer), which scale across 100,000+ third-party merchants, doubling live-streaming conversion rates and dramatically expanding automated advertising bids. 3P marketplace transactions rise to account for over 55% of total platform GMV, unlocking high-margin ad fees and cloud fulfillment commissions.

Simultaneously, dramatic CapEx efficiency and operational leverage materialize across JD's 1,600+ warehouse network. AI-driven route optimization, autonomous last-mile delivery, and robotics automation boost Free Cash Flow conversion well above GAAP net income. New Businesses (international supply chain corridors and local services) achieve rapid operating loss containment, crossing into aggregate segment operating breakeven by Year 4 as route density scales in overseas fulfillment hubs.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Annual active customer accounts reach 850 million (3.9% CAGR), with spend per customer climbing to $325 USD. 3P marketplace and advertising revenues compound at a 15% CAGR to reach $29.5B USD (12.0% of total revenue). JD Logistics external enterprise revenue grows at 12% annually. Group net revenue grows at a 6.2% CAGR, reaching $253.5B USD by Year 5.

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Gross margin expands 191 bps to 18.50% by Year 5. JD Logistics operating margin expands from 2.40% to 5.00% on high last-mile parcel density. Group operating margin reaches 4.60% ($11.66B USD). Automated fulfillment reduces required Maintenance CapEx to $1,250M USD despite volume expansion. Core Operating Owner Earnings jump from $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS on 1,340M ADSs) to $8,850M USD ($6.60 per ADS baseline; >$8.00 per ADS post-buyback retirements). Backed by $22,534M in Net Surplus Cash ($16.82 per ADS), capital return yields accelerate.

Key Milestones to Watch: 3P GMV share crossing 55%; adoption of JoyInsight/JD Streamer exceeding 100,000 active sellers; New Businesses reaching quarterly operating breakeven; Cash Conversion Cycle improving beyond -21.0 days.

📖 Story 3: Persistent Deflation, Subsidy Expiration Drag & New Business Burn (Bear Case)

In this downside stress scenario, structural consumer wage stagnation and the expiration of government trade-in subsidies plunge 1P Electronics and Appliances into a multi-year contraction worse than Q2 2026's -11.8% YoY decline. Growth in General Merchandise (+5.6% in Q2 2026) decelerates to low single digits, failing to offset durables softness. Price wars with low-cost aggregators force JD to fund aggressive, margin-dilutive price subsidies to defend platform volume.

Compounding retail margin compression, management fails to contain spending in New Businesses. Uncontrolled capital allocation into cross-border logistics and food delivery leads to runaway operating losses exceeding RMB 12.0B per quarter (>RMB 48B annual drag). CapEx efficiency suffers severe degradation: underutilized warehouse capacity creates negative operating leverage, route density drag spikes last-mile unit costs, and FCF conversion deteriorates. Structural RMB depreciation (slumping to 7.84 RMB/USD) further drags USD-denominated owner earnings.

Operational Metric Drivers & Revenue: Active customers stagnate at 680 million, with average spend per buyer falling 5% in local currency. Consolidated revenue in RMB crawls forward at a 1.5% CAGR, but converts into a USD contraction from $187.6B LTM to $178.5B USD by Year 5 at stressed FX rates.

Cost Dynamics, CapEx & Owner Earnings: Gross margin compresses to 15.50% as promotional price-matching erodes 1P markups. Fixed overhead across 32 million square meters of logistics space causes operating deleverage, dragging JD Logistics margins to 0.80%. Runaway New Business losses (>RMB 12.0B/qtr) depress group operating margin to 1.50% ($2.68B USD). Despite austerity CapEx cuts (Maintenance CapEx trimmed to $900M), Core Operating Owner Earnings drop from $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS on 1,340M ADSs) to $2,450M USD ($1.83 per ADS). Crucially, even under this extreme macroeconomic stress, the $22,534M Net Surplus Cash balance ($16.82 per ADS across 1,340M ADSs) establishes an absolute valuation floor.

Key Milestones to Watch: Gross margin falling below 15.0%; New Business losses exceeding RMB 12.0B/quarter; 1P Electronics/Appliances contracting >10% YoY for consecutive quarters; Cash Conversion Cycle elongating above -12.0 days.

🎯 Probability-Weighted Expected Value Synthesis

To avoid false precision or anchoring solely on a single operational path, we synthesize the three scenario valuations across 1,340M diluted ADSs into an institutional expected value:

  • Story 1 (Base Case - 50% Underwriting Probability): $71.60 / share
  • Story 2 (Bull Case - 25% High-Monetization Probability): $92.74 / share
  • Story 3 (Bear Case - 25% Structural Drag Probability): $38.99 / share

Probability-Weighted Expected Fair Value: $68.73 / share (Margin of Safety: 57.3% discount vs. today's market price of $29.35, representing a ~134% upside potential).

Sensitivity Note: Under an equal-weighted (33/33/33) distribution, Expected Fair Value is $67.78 / share.

Step-by-Step Mathematical Proofs Across the 3 Paths

Story 1 Proof (Base Case - Supply Chain Compounding, AI Merchant Tools & Loss Containment):

Starting with baseline Owner Earnings (\(OE_0\)) of $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS across 1,340M diluted ADSs) and compounding at ~7.5% per annum yields Year 5 Owner Earnings of $6,150M. Discounting Years 1–5 cash flows at a 9.5% hurdle rate generates an explicit present value of $20,270M ($15.13 per ADS, representing 27.6% of Operating EV). Capitalizing Year 5 Owner Earnings ($6,150M) at a 2.0% terminal growth rate (13.6x implied exit multiple) generates a terminal present value of $53,130M ($39.65 per ADS, representing 72.4% of Operating EV). Combining these yields an Operating Enterprise Value of $73,401M ($54.78 per ADS). Adding unencumbered net surplus balance sheet cash of $22,534M (+$16.82 per ADS based on $26.72B liquid cash, -$4.69B operational working capital buffer, -$2.17B tax haircut, -$10.17B funded debt, and +$5.98B equity affiliates) results in an Intrinsic Fair Value of $71.60 per ADS. Under a conservative 10.0x exit multiple floor, intrinsic fair value is $61.10 per ADS.

Story 2 Proof (Bull Case - Platform Monetization Flywheel & Logistics Automation Efficiency):

Starting with baseline \(OE_0\) of $4,282M ($3.20 per ADS) and compounding at ~15.6% per annum yields Year 5 Owner Earnings of $8,851M. Discounting Years 1–5 cash flows at 9.5% yields an explicit present value of $25,284M ($18.87 per ADS, representing 24.9% of Operating EV). Capitalizing Year 5 Owner Earnings at a 2.0% terminal growth rate (13.6x exit multiple) generates a terminal present value of $76,456M ($57.06 per ADS, representing 75.1% of Operating EV). Combining these yields an Operating Enterprise Value of $101,740M ($75.92 per ADS). Adding unencumbered net surplus balance sheet cash of $22,534M (+$16.82 per ADS across 1,340M ADSs) results in an Intrinsic Fair Value of $92.74 per ADS ($77.64 per ADS under a 10.0x exit floor).

Key Structural Takeaways from Wall Street Divergence

  • 100% Stock-Based Compensation Cash Deduction: Sell-side consensus models routinely add back Stock-Based Compensation ($680M LTM) as a "non-cash" expense under Non-GAAP net income. We treat SBC as an authentic cash cost that dilutes owner value and must be subtracted in full.
  • Maintenance vs. Growth CapEx & Logistics Obsolescence: While sell-side consensus models assume most CapEx generates net future growth, our framework accounts for ongoing fulfillment technology upkeep, automated sorting replacements, and delivery fleet maintenance as mandatory Maintenance CapEx ($1,050M LTM).
  • Disciplined Hurdle Rates vs. Low CAPM Discount Rates: Sell-side DCF models often employ low 7.0%–8.0% discount rates based on academic CAPM Betas. We demand a disciplined 9.5%–10.5% equity hurdle rate reflecting true opportunity cost, currency risk, and cross-border holding friction.
  • Multi-Layer Balance Sheet Net Cash Haircuts: Consensus models frequently credit gross cash without operational deductions or apply arbitrary low multiples to the entire business due to geopolitical headlines. We explicitly haircut balance sheet liquidity for operational working capital buffers (2.5% of net revenues, or $4.69B) and foreign remittance tax friction (7.5% withholding tax, or $2.17B), while fully adding back equity affiliates ($5.98B) to arrive at a rock-solid Net Surplus Cash bridge of +$16.82/ADS ($22,534M total).
